reviews.title: Helpful but Flawed
reviews.text:
Couple does a good job of what it says on the tin in terms of blocking apps. It also affords flexibility for you to exclude apps that you don’t want blocked and to set different rules for filters and scheduling. The UI is reasonably intuitive. However, there’s a lot of overreach by default, utilizing an all-or-nothing kind of approach. For example, if you’ve blocked Facebook, you can’t use any app or site that uses Facebook to login, even on the back end. You have to turn off the applicable rule entirely to regain that access; you can’t just pause the rule to execute the transaction.

Also, Opal will automatically sweep up apps its algorithm considers distracting, sometimes grabbing apps not originally included in its initial settings, but that it has decided are too distracting for you to access. You have to do a lot of fiddly configuration to exclude apps that you need to access. If you do not intentionally exclude an app from Opal, it is fair game for Opal to block without notice. Depending on your particular focus needs, that may be a feature, not a bug. I acknowledge spending a lot of effort to customize settings isn’t something I wanted to spend much time on.

Finally and most concerning, after I had used it for about a month and a half, I hit a bug where Opal just blocked everything and would not turn off or allow a pause. It effectively bricked everything but email and phone functionality. Rebooting the app and then the phone didn’t change anything. I had to delete Opal entirely and then re-install it, which wiped out my progress. Now, I’m not too invested in acquiring different gemstones, which is Opal’s reward pathway. But it was annoying to have to go through all this hassle to just restore my phone’s function.

At the end of the day, it’s still useful, plus I had invested in an annual subscription. But I don’t trust it entirely now. If it bricks me again, I will probably look for another solution.

reviews.title: Great for the most part
reviews.text:
My rating is actually a 3.5, but high enough swaying power to want to round it up to 4 stars. Overall this app has been helpful to block apps and aid in regaining my focus. There are 4 things however that prevent me from wanting to give it a 5 star rating:
1. Opal is pretty much social media focused, and automatically labels any social media and shopping adjacent apps as “distracting” and all others as “productive”—a very black and white approach—without taking into account your personal usage/lifestyle. This means that if you have to use a “distracting” app for work/school/project, it will count against you as being unproductive. On the (negative) flip side, mobile games are considered “productive” so if your main problem is that you’re spending time on your phone playing app game, Opal won’t dock you for it so you’ll have to manually set up timers to lock those specific apps. Considering we live in a time of technology where more and more things are being relegated to online, having this black and white approach is not a good business model.
2. The pomodoro timer has always been a great work tool, and Opal also lets you block apps during the timer, but the main issue is that when the timer is up there’s no alarm or any sort of sound that alerts you to take a break. This basically defeats the whole purpose of a work flow when you’re also having to take time to check the timer, or if you use it to *only* spend a certain amount of time on one task and  need the timer to go off and signal you to start a new task.
3. It will randomly list apps as “distracting” at the most random times. Every so often I’ll have to check my distracting apps list because there have been times where I’ve seen apps blocked that I only access like once every other month, or even (most recently in this case) apps that I don’t even have downloaded on my phone and have never used/seen before.
4. There used to be a time where Opal paired with the Focus modes on the actual phone, and in the phone settings you can set the Focus modes to link directly to Opal and automatically block distracting apps when you turned a specific Focus on. In one of the recent updates it stopped directly linking, so even though it’s still set up that way on my phone settings, Opal stopped automatically locking the apps with the Focus mode so I’ve had to go in and manually set rules up to lock at certain times.

reviews.text:
I actually do appreciate Opal, in general. It’s definitely helped me cut down on screentime. Was disappointed tho, that they’re taking the typical bogus approach to customer service by making themselves as unreachable to customers as possible. All I wanted was to send a quick message to the design team, and got stuck in some loop of community forums. I am not wasting my time on that BS. Seems rather ironic that a company claiming to help keep people off their screens would add layers of app garbage for what could just be a simple contact form— click and send. Disappointing. 

And all I had to say, as feedback, was that the backdrop has switched to an ocean scene, but it’s clearly something like AI. The sound doesn’t align with the scene, and it’s clearly a split screen-the same waves mirrored on both sides. Believe me, your customers do spend enough time in nature to know the difference between real ocean and fake. And I will not support AI in any way shape or form, so if this continues, you’ll have lost me. 

There’s also no way to mute the fake ocean sounds. If I’m checking my apps in public, I don’t need extra noise. Design a way to permanently mute the sounds in settings. And don’t waste our time with useless customer service blocks. It just tells me you’re eating up over $100 a year without wanting to actually serve your customers.

reviews.title: I miss the old Opal
reviews.text:
I don’t ever write reviews, but I just want to say when I found opal it was the best app I’ve ever downloaded. It was perfect for screen time monitoring and blocking. It used to be very easy to use and navigate. You used to be able to organize your apps by least to most distracting and also remove certain apps like Navigation/GPS or Music from your screen time. 

Now, everything is counted in your screen time, and even if I’m not using an app but it’s running in the background, like Life360, it counts that as screen time, which, sorry, is kind of absurd. I’m obviously not scrolling on life360 for fourteen hours. 

Also, since the big Opal update a few weeks or months back, certain features just haven’t been working as they used to, and the interface is much more confusing. Sometimes my gems don’t show up on the Home Screen— it’s just empty. For a few days my streak was set back to zero (which was fixed). The app is much more laggy now and sometimes crashes when I try to open it or when I try to unblock an app temporarily. 

One more thing— if you have a time limit rule for an app, say you set YouTube to be allowed for an hour a day, it seems that Opal just counts down from the time that you open the app now rather than monitoring when you’re on or off the app. I personally set my YouTube for 30 mins on certain days, and even if I just open it, watch a video, and exit the app, I’ll still get a notification a half hour later saying that it’s blocked again. 

There’s also a bug or glitch with that particular YouTube rule I think because when it notifies me for “15 mins left” it spams that notification and my phone keeps buzzing every two seconds. I end up having to mute all notifications from the app because it’s so incessant.  

I know you guys aren’t actually going to fix a lot of this stuff because with the nature of using apples interface for recording screen time data, you can’t. I just wanted to put this out there in case some of these issues are fixable. Thank you.

reviews.title: Bring back exclusions
reviews.text: I started using this app 12/25, and it was a total game changer for my ADHD. However, it has slowly become less and less effective for me with all the changes and updates. I used to be so proud of my screen time- it was sort of gamified for me, seeing how low I could keep it. There used to be a feature to exclude apps from being included in your screen time, which was a big part of what made the app so effective for me. I was always discouraged seeing a high screen time on my device from apps like maps or Spotify or my audiobook apps, especially because I often forgot to lock my phone. Opal gave you the option to exclude those from contributing to your screen time. I also use a row counting app when I crochet, and it was great to exclude that because I have it open for hours at a time. When the feature was taken away, it was really discouraging to see my screen time shoot up. All of a sudden just having my row counting app open shot my screen time up by hours. Having time that is EXPLICITLY analog and intentionally offline contribute to a previously motivating feature was such a bummer. I feel like the app worked well initially, all of these extra features and changes make it much more unusable for me. I think all of the rapid changes should be introduced slowly. When people find something that works, especially people struggling with attention, the apps influx of changes can be frustrating and render the app less effective. Don’t make changes for changes sake.

Another thing that sets this apart from screen time limits, is the small, but effective amount of effort you need in order to reset your limit. If you want to reset it, you have to go to the app, and wait 5 seconds, while it plays a nice ambience on the screen. It’s a nice touch. The second time you reset, it’s 40 seconds. I’ve only ever gotten to that one twice. It’s a very effective system. And you need to show a friend a video, or message someone, there are ways to bypass it. I also love the little achievement gems you get. You have a little collection shelf in the app, and they are actually really neat to look at. Great app, and a lot of features aren’t locked behind a paywall.

reviews.title: It was great until the paywall
reviews.text: I honestly enjoyed the previous versions of the app and it helped me reclaim my time and my life from social media. The app as it was before was extremely useful and had a generous free version that I recommended to friends and family. That said, I would have gladly given the previous version five stars, but as it stands now, the free version has lost much of what made it so valuable, so I can only give it two. Without the $19.99/month subscription, you’re limited to creating a single rule, along with several other restrictions. If the monthly pricing were more reasonable, I could justify subscribing. Likewise, not everyone can justify paying $99.99 upfront for a year or $399 for a lifetime subscription. I understand that the developers need to make a living, but I hope they reassess the balance of the free and paid versions to make it more accessible to a wider variety of people rather than commodifying wellbeing into a luxury. I really do think this app could help a lot of people, but not at the current pricing.

reviews.title: Lost access to all apps upon arriving in a foreign country
reviews.text:
I wanted to love this app, and it worked well for me for a couple of months. Unfortunately, I had a serious experience while traveling. After landing late at night in a foreign country, I needed to use my phone to order an Uber.  I tried using the typical “15 min break from blocks” like I normally would to access my apps after bedtime, and it simply wouldn’t work. I tried sending a message to customer service for help, but it was also blocking my email app. I dug through the app and found  the “emergency pass” which I’d never seen before, but when I clicked on it said I’d already used up all of my “emergency passes.” I tried deleting the app, but even that didn’t work! Something was still running in the background and later ChatGPT helped me remove it. Eventually i figured out how to  override the features on my phone through the iPhone setting “allow apps at all times.” 

After returning home, I also had difficulty removing the app completely from my phone and computer, experiencing login/verification issues when trying to access my account.

Support told me this occurred because it was an older version of the app and that it has since been redesigned. I hope that’s true. However, because the failure involved the Emergency Pass itself - the feature intended for situations exactly like this - I don’t feel comfortable relying on any version of the app. 

If you use Opal, I strongly recommend throughly testing all emergency features before depending on them while traveling or in any situation where you may need immediate or emergency access to your phone.

reviews.text: i’m glad that i’m seeing other people having the same issue as me. i’ve been using opal for about 2 years and ive loved it up until now. the new update has consistently made my entire phone overheat and crash upon trying to open and use the app, the blockers aren’t working like they should (either not blocking at the correct times or staying blocked for longer than i want), and i really don’t like all the notifications. i’m disappointed that an app that worked so well for me before could be ruined so quickly. i wish there was a way for me to go back on it.

reviews.title: Too many changes
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app pretty much since it was released and I’m really disappointed with the quality of all the new updates. The UI is extremely busy and doesn’t seem to make sense, I can’t set my blocks to fully “quit” after I wait a certain amount of time, and I’m only on 5 second blockers, the amount of waiting time doesn’t increase with each attempt. I had to log back in again and it completely lost all the rules I had setup for years, leading me thru the tutorial, but still kept my streaks - even though my hourly stats were gone. I used to talk about this app to EVERYBODY I met and happily paid the yearly subscription but now I don’t know what’s going on with this app. Such a huge overhaul should’ve meant that all the features would be coming back, not weeks or months down the road. Super disappointed, I hope Opal improves soon
